annotations.text:
Seven controls on a blank page, five of them switched off. The bar keeps its full shape and dims what cannot act yet, rather than hiding it.

Bar: Again, undo, settled, you.
Foot: cross off, settle, camera, search — the same four at every width.

No rule above the foot. shell.tsx has no border-t anywhere, and Notes has none either: space does the separating.

Every capture carries text. A photograph opens a line with the image on it and the caret waiting; it is not a capture until it is captioned.

So a picture never costs the page its rhythm — the image rides the line in the same slot a resolved year takes, and one line is still one line.

Undo and the × are not the same gesture.

Undo DELETES — the one exception to "nothing is ever deleted", bounded in SQL to ten seconds from created_at, for a line that should never have existed.

The × writes `dropped` — a resolution, not a delete. The row stays where it is, struck through, and the same × puts it back.

The page is not a text buffer. Only the bottom line is live; every line above it is a record, so tapping one has exactly one meaning — pick it.

Second tap edits. The brass bar sits in the gutter, not in the text: the caret’s width and colour, without claiming a character position.

Keyboard follows liveness — up on a cold open, gone the moment you pick a saved line.

Reading back is narrowing, not sorting. The tray takes settled things off the page, search finds what you can name, and the days make what is left navigable by memory.

Nothing else is available in Phase 1: type exists only for resolved lines, location is Phase 5, and manufacturing the signal means asking people to categorise.
